text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* The Constitutional Court rejected a request for referendum to scrap a proportional representation part of the electoral system, sparking heated political debate. The Court gave the green light to 11 other votes later this year, including one seeking to abolish the use of "golden shares" that give the Treasury special powers in privatised companies (all).
* The cabinet approved a package of emergency measures including cheap loans for the dairy sector to help farmers hit by EU fines for milk overproduction (all).
* A year-long corruption trial of former prime minister and current opposition leader Silvio Berlusconi was declared null and void and will start again from scratch (all).
*Industrial giant Fiat's operating profits fell in 1996 to around 1.8 trillion lire from 3.235 trillion lire in 1995. Annual sales rose three percent to around 78 trillion lire (all).
* The cabinet has approved a report on motorway operator Autostrade by Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi concerning the criteria for the group's privatisation, which is planned by June (all).
* Carlo De Benedetti's industrial holding CIR sold shares in information technology group Olivetti on the market, bringing its current stake down to 9.3 percent (all).

* Telecom Italia appointed credit institutes IMI Spa and Deutsche Morgan Grenfell to evaluate state telecoms group Stet and Telecom and recommend the appropriate share swap ratio. Stet and Telecom are to merge ahead of the group's planned privatisation, with Telecom incorporated into Stet. Tomaso Tommasi di Vignano, new managing director of Stet, was co-opted as a member of Telecom Italia board (all).
* The price of train tickets will rise by 2.5 percent starting on March 1 (all).
** Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
